paradigm.value: vt2: the rare wrist is always the right wrist and always the target (ANN18)
paradigm.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). (GUG18). The frozen VT2 follows ANN18 instead: 'instructed to mentally count the stimuli presented on the right wrist' (ANN18 Methods).
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (Front Neurosci 12:370; PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

timing.value: mur20: 100-ms pulse + 100-ms pause (SOA 200 ms), 4 instruction pauses of 13.5 s [derived], run ~157 s
timing.quote: GUG18 states the pulse and the run length but not the ISI or the pause length: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' MUR20 supplies the pause: 'All vibrotactile stimuli lasted 100 ms with a 100 ms pause between stimuli. The whole paradigm (i.e., one run) required around 2.5 min per run.' Consistent with every GUG18-stated timing item.
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; MUR20 (PMC7161577), Methods 'Paradigm' (cat. §4a)

feat.value: seg8: −100 to 600 ms, 8 equal-segment means, no baseline
feat.quote: Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4a); baseline NOT STATED

summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

thr.value: gt23: accuracy > 0.23
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c)

summary.value: median of the 30-point accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

feat.value: seg8: −100 to 600 ms, 8 equal-segment means, no baseline
feat.quote: Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4a); baseline NOT STATED

summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. summary.value: the full-test-pool point of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

ANN18: 'The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.' ds7 departs from GUG18's stated 8 segments over −100 to 600 ms.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods (cat. §4a)

summary.value: the maximum of the accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

thr.value: binom_n30: accuracy >= 0.2667 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 30 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 26.7% departs from it. Source of n = 30: CH18 §2.5: 'We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).' CONTRADICTS stands: no grid variant uses CH18's VTP design ('duration = 110 ms, ISI = 300 ms', §2.3.3) or its features ('an average was performed on every 12 samples for each EEG channel, resulting in 15 new sample points', §2.4), so the variant pairs CH18's n with GUG18 / MUR20 / ANN18 settings, against GUG18's stated 23%.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c); CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.3.3, §2.4, §2.5

The frozen VT2 follows ANN18 instead: 'instructed to mentally count the stimuli presented on the right wrist' (ANN18 Methods).
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (Front Neurosci 12:370; PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

feat.value: ds7: 0 to 600 ms down-sampled to 7, baseline −100 to 0 ms (ANN18)
feat.quote: GUG18: 'Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.' ANN18: 'The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.' ds7 departs from GUG18's stated 8 segments over −100 to 600 ms.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods (cat. §4a)

summary.value: median of the 30-point accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

thr.value: binom_n30: accuracy >= 0.2667 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 30 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 26.7% departs from it. Source of n = 30: CH18 §2.5: 'We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).' CONTRADICTS stands: no grid variant uses CH18's VTP design ('duration = 110 ms, ISI = 300 ms', §2.3.3) or its features ('an average was performed on every 12 samples for each EEG channel, resulting in 15 new sample points', §2.4), so the variant pairs CH18's n with GUG18 / MUR20 / ANN18 settings, against GUG18's stated 23%.
thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c); CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.3.3, §2.4, §2.5

paradigm.quote: Abstract: '(ii) VT3 with three vibro-tactile stimulators fixed on both wrists and on the back'. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4a); baseline NOT STATED

summary.value: median of the 30-point accuracy curve
summary.quote: Which summary of the accuracy curve is reported per run is NOT STATED. GUG18 Table 2 caption: 'Median classification accuracies are shown for VT2 and VT3 assessment sessions for 12 UWS patients.' but its 'Median' row is the arithmetic mean of the run rows [derived: VT2, 15 runs summing to 575 = 38.33, printed 38.3, true median 30; VT3, 24 runs summing to 630 = 26.25, printed 26.3, true median 17.5]. MUR20 Discussion: 'Two recent studies reported a median classification of 26% ( Guger et al., 2018 )'. GUG17 Figure 2 legend: 'The number presented in the top right of each accuracy plot is the mean accuracy.' CH18 §2.4 describes yet another score: 'The scores are summed up to provide the classification accuracy (e.g., 0/30 = 0%, 30/30 = 100%). The shuffling and classification were then repeated 10 times and results were averaged to obtain the assessment accuracy'. The 'median' label therefore does not fix the curve point (checker finding); the earlier granularity argument (5/15/25/45%) is withdrawn as not decisive, since it relies on reps = 10 taken from GUG17 / MUR20.
summary.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Table 2; MUR20 (Front Neurosci 14:294; PMC7161577), Discussion; GUG17 (Front Neurosci 11:251; PMC5418541), Figure 2 legend; CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.4 (cat. §4b)

thr.value: binom_n30: accuracy >= 0.2667 (one-sided 5% binomial bar at p0 = 1/8 for n = 30 [derived])
thr.quote: A discriminable response was defined as a classification accuracy above 23% for VT2 and VT3 assessment (i.e., suggesting target vs. non-target ERPs could be discriminated). 23% is the 95% confidence interval tested with a binomial test. The n behind the bar is NOT STATED, but the bar itself is: 23%. A bar of 26.7% departs from it. Source of n = 30: CH18 §2.5: 'We calculated the p value and considered a response to be significantly different from chance if it was associated with p < .05 (n = 30 trials for AEP and VTP; n = 60 for MoI and MoA; chance success rate = 1/8 for AEP and VTP; 1/2 for MoI and MoA (Combrisson and Jerbi, 2015)).' thr.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification' (cat. §4c); CH18 (Clin Neurophysiol 129:1519; PMC6045427), §2.3.3, §2.4, §2.5

paradigm.value: vt3: per group 1 left + 1 right + 6 distractors, instructed wrist = target, 2 left / 2 right instructions
paradigm.quote: Abstract: '(ii) VT3 with three vibro-tactile stimulators fixed on both wrists and on the back'. Methods: 'In both VT3 modes, one additional stimulator is fixed on the back or shoulder as a distractor, which is active in 75% of stimulations. The other two stimulators are again fixed on the right and left wrist and each receive 12.5% of the stimuli.' The per-group composition and the pseudo-random, balanced target wrist are as stated; the group count (stated 30 groups, 15 left and 15 right targets; built 60 groups, 30 and 30) is a constant departure: see constant_departures.mbvt 'groups per run'.
paradigm.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Abstract and Methods 'BCI assessment' (cat. §4a)

timing.value: ann18: 30-ms pulse, SOA 300 ms, no instruction pause (instr = 0 s), 480 stimuli in 144 s
timing.quote: GUG18: 'During stimulus presentation, the BCI system activates the vibro-tactile stimulation for 100 ms on the left or right wrist (also chosen pseudo-randomly)' and 'Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. During both the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, each run lasted about 2.5 min.' ANN18: 'mechanical vibrations with a frequency of 225 Hz, which lasted for 30 ms, with an inter-stimulus interval of 270 ms. A total of 480 stimuli were presented, resulting in a paradigm duration of 2.4 min.' The 30-ms pulse departs from GUG18's stated 100 ms and the zero pause departs from GUG18's stated pause before each target wrist (ANN18's own VT3 also instructs per block: 'The subject was instructed through headphones which hand to attend for every block').
timing.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'BCI assessment'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods 'BCI assessment and data processing' (cat. §4a)

feat.value: ds7: 0 to 600 ms down-sampled to 7, baseline −100 to 0 ms (ANN18)
feat.quote: GUG18: 'Across all paradigms, we extracted data epochs of −100–600 ms around each stimulus and rejected trials in which the amplitude of the EEG signal exceeds ±100 μV. Each of these 700 ms data epochs was then sub-divided into 8 data segments of equal duration. We then created sub-averages for each of these data segments.' ANN18: 'The 600 ms after stimulus onset was down sampled to 7 samples.' ds7 departs from GUG18's stated 8 segments over −100 to 600 ms.
feat.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093; no printed pages accessible), Methods 'Data analysis and classification'; ANN18 (PMC5992287), Methods (cat. §4a)

The benchmark endpoint for every main-set pipeline is evidence of top-down engagement (the command-following call); CH13 states that a non-discriminative target response vs baseline is bottom-up orienting, so a call on it departs from the paper (checker finding).
rule.source: CH13 (NeuroImage Clin 3:450-461), Abstract and General discussion (cat. §2)

clust.value: ms40: clusters of >= 40 ms
clust.quote: Paper p.452: 'sampled at 250 Hz'; corrclust.m l. 6: clustsize 10; plotgfp.m l. 48 drops clusters spanning fewer than 10 points of a 4-ms grid. 10 samples at the stated 250 Hz = 40 ms [derived]; the two readings coincide at 250 Hz and differ at other rates.
clust.source: CH13-CODE (corrclust.m l. 6, plotgfp.m l. 48); CH13 (NeuroImage Clin 3:450-461) p.452

reject.value: zvar: epochs whose maximum channel variance has z > 3 rejected (automated)
reject.quote: p.452: 'Data containing excessive eye movement or muscular artefact were rejected by a quasi-automated procedure: noisy channels and epochs were identified by calculating their normalised variance and then manually rejected or retained by visual confirmation.' Inline Supplementary Table S2 ('Trials rejected'): 0 to 191 per participant (0 in HV4, HV5, HV6). zvar automates the stated variance criterion; the z > 3 bar is ours and the visual confirmation cannot be reproduced.
reject.source: CH13 (NeuroImage Clin 3:450-461) p.452; PMC3830059 Inline Supplementary Table S2 (cat. §2)

n_blocks.value: 12 blocks (fits the 1505-s window of a 30-min BDSP segment)
n_blocks.quote: p.451: 'The experiment comprised of 20 blocks (lasting approx. 1.5 min each) of binaurally presented word stimuli'. Reason: 20 blocks need a 2530-s window, which a 30-min BDSP segment cannot hold; 12 blocks (1505 s) is the length shortened to fit, with the block design, timing and statistics unchanged. Not eligible for the stated-rule headline; reported in the 'shortened to fit' row.

mbvt.stated_value: 30 groups of 8; 15 left-target and 15 right-target groups (GUG18; the same paragraph also implies 4 x (15 + 105) = 480 stimuli)
mbvt.quote: In the VT2 and VT3 assessment paradigms, the target wrist is selected pseudo-randomly, and each run has an equal number of left and right targets (15 each). | Each subject received 15 target stimulations and 7 × 15 non-target stimulations prior to a brief pause as an instruction to focus on the upcoming target wrist. | Each VT2 run contained 30 groups of eight stimuli (120 left, 120 right). Each VT3 run contains 30 groups of 8 stimuli (30 left, 30 right, 180 distractors).
mbvt.source: GUG18 (Front Neurosci 12:423; PMC6034093), Methods 'BCI assessment' (three sentences of one paragraph, separated by ' | ')
mbvt.our_value: 60 groups (4 instructions x 15 groups, 480 stimuli; GUG17 'performs this task four times', MUR20 '480 stimuli per run, with 60 groups of 8 stimuli'): 30 left-target and 30 right-target groups in VT3, a 30-point test curve
mbvt.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); GUG18 is internally inconsistent here, and the curve length changes the null distribution of every summary

mbvt.stated_value: Fz, C3, Cz, C4, CP1, CPz, CP2, Pz (8)
mbvt.quote: The EEG electrodes used for the experiments were positioned at sites Fz, C3, Cz, C4, CP1, CPz, CP2, and Pz according to the extended International 10–20 System.
mbvt.our_value: Fz, C3, Cz, C4, P3, Pz, P4 (7): CP1 -> P3, CP2 -> P4, CPz -> Pz (duplicate dropped) in 10-20 data
mbvt.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); expected small on a null (no evoked signal at any site); one fewer channel means fewer LDA features

mbvt.quote: The reference electrode was fixed on the right earlobe and the ground electrode was mounted on the forehead.
mbvt.our_value: the recording's own reference (BDSP / source montage), not re-referenced

mbvt.stated_value: remove target and non-target trials until the ratio is 1:7 again (MUR20)
mbvt.quote: After removal of trials with artifacts, we then removed target and non-target trials until the 1:7 ratio was maintained again.
mbvt.our_value: a whole group of 8 is dropped when any of its epochs is rejected (keeps 1:7 exactly; which trials MUR20 removed is NOT STATED)
mbvt.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); differs only on recordings with rejected epochs

chennu13.stated_value: 128-channel EGI net, vertex reference; 91 scalp channels retained; average reference
chennu13.quote: During the experiment, 128-channel high-density EEG data in microvolts (μV), sampled at 250 Hz and referenced to the vertex, were collected using the Net Amps 300 amplifier (Electrical Geodesics Inc., Oregon, USA). Data from 91 channels over the scalp surface (at locations shown in Fig. 1B, top) were retained for further analysis.
chennu13.our_value: the 19 10-20 channels, average reference over those 19
chennu13.likely_direction: likely LOWER false-call rate than with 91 channels for the condition-vs-own-baseline GFP rules: in my scratch simulations (cat. §2 null notes) more spatial degrees of freedom raised that test's null rate; not measured on real EEG. The TCT and the explicit-vs-implicit test: unknown (not measured)

chennu13.stated_value: Infomax ICA, noisy components rejected visually (5-47 per participant, Table S2)
chennu13.quote: Independent Components Analysis (ICA) based on the Infomax ICA algorithm (Bell and Sejnowski, 1995) was used to visually identify and reject noisy components.
chennu13.source: CH13 (NeuroImage Clin 3:450-461) p.452; PMC3830059 Inline Supplementary Table S2
chennu13.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); residual artefact is not locked to the overlaid markers

chennu13.stated_value: rejected channels interpolated by spherical splines
chennu13.quote: Finally, previously rejected channels were interpolated using spherical spline interpolation, and data were re-referenced to the average of all channels.
During the experiment, 128-channel high-density EEG data in microvolts (μV), sampled at 250 Hz
chennu13.our_value: the recording's native rate (no resampling); the cluster-length consequence is the 'clust' axis

gibson16.stated_value: FC1, Fz, FC2, C3, Cz, C4, CP1, CP2, Pz, Oz, PO7, PO8 (12)
gibson16.quote: EEG data were recorded at sites FC1, Fz, FC2, C3, Cz, C4, CP1, CP2, Pz, Oz, PO7, and PO8 using an electrode cap with the g.Gamma active electrode system
gibson16.source: GIB16 author accepted manuscript (Kent KAR), 'Page n of 42' p.7
gibson16.our_value: 13 nearest 10-20 sites: F3, Fz, F4, C3, Cz, C4, P3, P4, Pz, O1, O2, T5, T6 (FC1 -> F3, FC2 -> F4, CP1 -> P3, CP2 -> P4, Oz -> O1 and O2, PO7 -> T5, PO8 -> T6)
gibson16.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); the cluster tests' spatial neighbourhoods are wider apart; the SSEP test reads Pz, which exists

gibson16.quote: The recordings were referenced to the right earlobe with a forehead (Fpz) ground.
gibson16.source: GIB16 author accepted manuscript (Kent KAR), 'Page n of 42' p.7
gibson16.our_value: the recording's own reference, not re-referenced

gibson16.stated_value: kurtosis computed for each stimulus type separately, trials beyond 2.5 SD rejected
gibson16.quote: In a second step, the kurtosis of the signal across all channels was calculated for each stimulus type separately, and all trials exceeding 2.5 standard deviations of the mean were rejected.
gibson16.source: GIB16 author accepted manuscript (Kent KAR), 'Page n of 42' p.7
gibson16.our_value: each trial's largest channel kurtosis, z-scored over ALL kept trials pooled across stimulus types
gibson16.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); expected small on a null, where the stimulus types do not differ

sokoliuk21.stated_value: ICA to remove blinks and horizontal eye movements
sokoliuk21.quote: Then, data were visually inspected for artifacts as well as noisy channels, which were removed from the data before an ICA was computed, to remove blinks and horizontal eye movements from the data.
sokoliuk21.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); ITPC is amplitude-free, so ocular activity not locked to the trial onsets should mainly add phase noise [mine]

sokoliuk21.stated_value: re-referenced to average (Script_1 averages over all channels, including A1, A2, COMNT, SCALE)
sokoliuk21.quote: Finally, noisy channels were interpolated by using data of their neighbors, which were identified via the triangulation method, as implemented in FieldTrip, before the data were re-referenced to average.
sokoliuk21.source: SOK21 (Ann Neurol 89:646-656) p.650; SOK21-CODE (OSF wu2vy, Script_1 l. 325-329)
sokoliuk21.our_value: average over the 19 scalp channels only

sokoliuk21.stated_value: noisy channels interpolated from triangulated neighbours (same quote)
sokoliuk21.quote: Finally, noisy channels were interpolated by using data of their neighbors, which were identified via the triangulation method, as implemented in FieldTrip, before the data were re-referenced to average.

sokoliuk21.stated_value: filters at the recorded rate (256 or 512 Hz), then down-sampled to 256 Hz
sokoliuk21.quote: Subsequently, data were downsampled to 256 Hz to assure the same sampling rate for all recordings
sokoliuk21.our_value: recordings below 256 Hz are resampled to 256 Hz BEFORE the Script_1 filters (their 100-Hz edge is above a 128-Hz recording's Nyquist); filters run on the overlay span with edge padding, not the whole recording
sokoliuk21.likely_direction: unknown (not measured); expected negligible at the 0.78-3.12 Hz frequencies of interest

errata.where: the erp catalogue §6 (GIB16), SSEP F-test quote
errata.error: The catalogue quoted 'An F ratio (alpha=.05; F2,20>=3.49) was computed to compare the power at 5 and 10 Hz with the average power in the ten adjacent ~1 Hz frequency bins' and stopped before the parenthesis that names the bins. The frozen gibson16 module therefore treated the noise bins as NOT STATED and froze two readings ('plain', 'nonharm'), neither of which matches the stated set.
errata.aam_quote: An F ratio (alpha=.05; F2,20>=3.49) was computed to compare the power at 5 and 10 Hz with the average power in the ten adjacent ~1 Hz frequency bins (2-4 Hz, 6-9 Hz, and 11-13 Hz)39.
errata.source: GIB16 author accepted manuscript (Kent KAR), 'Page 8 of 42'
errata.consequence: All 4 gibson16 SSEP variants are CONTRADICTS on 'bins' (correction accepted by the lead). The catalogue file itself was not edited (read-only for this task).
